impact: Two teams (care2talk, CPM) on v1.7.1: when Codex rejects the model (see ISS-045 for the root cause: resumed chunks fall to the config.toml default), every review fails over to Gemini; the verdict comes back as a normal approve/request_changes and only the `models` array reveals which provider answered. Raw evidence from cpm-f2: after failover the models entry reads `"requested":null,"resolved":"Gemini 3.8 Flash (Medium)","observed":null,"evidence":"bridge_selection"` although the call passed model "gpt-6-astra" explicitly, and `provenance.warning` is null. Also `review_mode` reads "failover" on every result from the failover composite, including calls that resolved on the primary with no failover, so it cannot be used to detect one. Asks: the tool result carries the primary provider's classified error and the failover reason (e.g. `degraded: { provider, code, message }`); `requested` retains the caller's original value through failover; `review_mode` (or a new field) distinguishes "failover configured" from "failover occurred"; the "model not supported with a ChatGPT account" message gets its own classification. Related: ISS-030 (same blind spot in the deliberation composite), ISS-048.
resolution: Commit d1f8a20. Failover no longer drops the requested model: a tier is carried as-is and a tier-model is mapped back to its tier via tierForModel for the other provider (carriedModelForFailover). Results restore models[].requested and add a failover block {from, error, requested_model, carried_model}, present only when failover happened. SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS and README explain how to read it.
title: Failover hides the primary provider's error: unsupported Codex model silently routes every review to Gemini with no failover reason in the result
